title: Terminal dock
summary: Bottom dock of engine-owned PTY terminals (xterm.js) with Claude Code tabs, a Chat tab, an ask bar and a resize grip; open state and height are written before first paint. Backend: PTY sessions, WebSocket stream, loopback-only routes. From formlit.
description: Frontend `TerminalDock` builds its head, stage and ask bar once; tabs are added and removed one by one and the status note is patched in place. Its open state and height live on `documentElement` (`data-ft-dock`, `data-ft-dock-h`, `--ft-dock-size`), set before first paint by a second inline script in index.html (see `theme.prepaint-boot`), so `terminal.css` reserves the row and nothing moves on open. Backend `services/terminal.py` opens PTYs (ptyprocess on macOS and Linux, pywinpty on Windows) and `routers/terminal.py` exposes them under /api/terminal with an origin check, a 24-socket cap and a WebSocket per tab. The Chat tab is `ui.chat-pane`; the Claude Code launch path is `svc.claude-code-agents`. The engine owns every process. Imports ../io/api and ./i18n (not seeded).
statusReason: seeded from B06 for the owner to confirm

invariants.text: Build a node once, then patch text, classes, hidden flags and lists in place. Never assign innerHTML or clear textContent on a live container to rebuild it, and reserve space so nothing shifts when content arrives.
User-visible strings go through t() from the i18n module; the English text is the key.
Icons are inline currentColor SVG strings from the icons module (icon(name, size)); no icon library, and the three-star sparkle icon is banned under any name.

The engine is reached on loopback only, behind the app-wide LocalGuard middleware (app/core/local_guard.py, not in this corpus); routes that act (start processes, write settings or secrets, WebSockets) also check the request origin with require_local or origin_ok.
The open flag and height are on documentElement before first paint, written by the inline boot script; the component never reads them back after paint to size the row.
Every PTY and child process is owned and closed by the engine; the window only attaches to it over WebSocket.
WebSocket attachments go through take_socket/release_socket (24 at once).
